subject: Hosted API latency commitments — measurement window proposal & temporary carveout
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@finlogic.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: FinLogic Procurement <procurement@finlogic.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments for EU region (p50/p95)

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the predictable tail latency and the routing options. As we scope the legal language, procurement has raised a question about the measurement window and temporary exception handling for p95 in EU traffic.

Specifically:
- FinLogic needs to understand whether p95 will be measured on a rolling 30-day window or per-day aggregation (and how daypart spikes are handled).
- We also need a proposed operational carveout for controlled migrations (3 business days) and for major cloud provider incidents (how you evidence and exclude).
- Finally, our legal team asked whether Redwood will offer a temporary grace for p95 for the first two weeks of go-live while traffic patterns stabilize, and if so, what remediation commitments exist.

Can you send a short proposal and sample evidence we can attach to the contract? A one-page summary plus a sample query or CSV of how measurements look would be ideal.

Best,
Sara Li
Director, Platform Ops — FinLogic

Attachments: none

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Sara Li <sara.li@finlogic.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments for EU region (p50/p95)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Putting Lauren and Karthik on this thread; they're owning SLO policy and contracts respectively. Below is a short proposal and I'm attaching a draft evidence CSV and a two-page SLO summary (pdf).

Proposal (summary):
- Measurement: p50 and p95 computed on a rolling 7-day window, sampled daily and reported as daily rollups for contract visibility. Rolling window reduces sensitivity to single-day anomalies while preserving responsiveness to regressions.
- Aggregation: p50 = median latency per-request. p95 = 95th percentile computed across all requests in the rolling window. We will provide both per-region and global rollups; EU-specific metrics will be available.
- Dayparts and transient spikes: transient spikes shorter than 3 minutes that correlate with known model cache warmups or bursts are detectable by our anomaly heuristics and can be marked for review. Automated carveouts will not be automatic in the contract; instead we propose a documented evidence-and-review process (see below).
- Temporary grace for go-live: a 14-calendar-day stabilization grace for p95 where we do not apply financial remedies; during this period Redwood will provide daily remediation reports and priority runbook collaboration. If stability targets are not met by day 14, remediation milestones escalate per the SLA addendum.
- Formal carveouts: migration maintenance (up to 72 hours per major migration, pre-notified), verified cloud-provider outages (requires cloud incident report and our independent telemetry), and customer-triggered traffic shaping.

Evidence package (attached): sample CSV contains per-request timestamps, region, route, latency_ms, and a computed rolling window p95 column to show how values move over time.

Next steps:
1) Lauren — can you confirm whether rolling 7-day is defensible for FinLogic's regulatory needs or we should propose 30-day instead?
2) Karthik — if legal wants explicit wording for the 14-day stabilization grace, can you draft one paragraph we can attach?

Sara — if this aligns we'll produce a short addendum and a DocuSign-ready appendix.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-draft-20260611.pdf, slo-evidence-sample.csv

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, Sara Li <sara.li@finlogic.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments for EU region (p50/p95)

Sara — quick operational clarifications from our side. I want to be explicit about two practical items so expectations are set correctly: 

1) Measurement window choice: we recommend a 7-day rolling window for initial commercial SLAs because it balances sensitivity and noise and matches how our monitoring detects regressions. If FinLogic requires a longer contractual window (30 days), we can set the contract to 30 days with a 7-day operational alerting window used for incident response.

2) Carveout process: the evidence pack must include (a) Redwood telemetry export (we provide a signed CSV), (b) provider incident ticket id (when relevant), and (c) a short joint statement from both sides confirming the event timing. Upon submission we'll open an internal review that produces a final decision within 48 business hours.

3) Stabilization grace fine print: the 14-day grace starts on the first date that FinLogic flips production traffic to Redwood's hosted API. During grace we commit to daily status meetings and a prioritized runbook to remediate regressions. The grace does not apply to security incidents or misconfigured traffic that originates from FinLogic's environment.

I attached a one-page flow diagram in the PDF that outlines the review steps. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to run through the flow with your procurement/legal folks.

—Lauren
Principal Product Manager, SLOs & Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-draft-20260611.pdf

From: Sara Li <sara.li@finlogic.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments for EU region (p50/p95)

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/legal after internal review: 
- FinLogic prefers a 30-day contractual measurement window but accepts your 7-day operational alerting cadence as long as the contract explicitly states we will report both. 
- We need the carveout review turnaround shortened to 24 business hours if possible; our ops team requires decisions faster to avoid blocking rollouts. Is that feasible?
- For the 14-day grace, legal wants a clause that requires Redwood to submit a remediation plan within 48 hours of any p95 breach during the grace period, with concrete milestones.

If you can accept those three items we'll ask our legal to proceed with an addendum and get it into DocuSign. Would you be able to take a short call tomorrow to finalize language?

Best,
Sara

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Li <sara.li@finlogic.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments for EU region (p50/p95)

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. We can accommodate the three points with the following binding language suggestions for the addendum: 

1) Contract window: "p50 and p95 shall be measured and reported on both a rolling 7-day operational window (for alerting and incident response) and a contractual 30-day measurement window (for SLA compliance and remedies)."

2) Carveout review: "Upon submission of a carveout evidence package, Redwood shall provide an initial determination within 24 business hours and a final determination within 5 business days. If additional evidence is requested, the 24-hour initial determination may be provisional pending full review."

3) Grace remediation: "During the 14-calendar-day stabilization grace, if p95 exceeds the contractual threshold for a given day, Redwood will (a) provide an initial remediation plan within 48 hours, (b) escalate to weekly executive review if the breach persists beyond 7 days, and (c) apply the standard SLA remedies only if remediation milestones are not met per the agreed appendix."

We will update the draft addendum and place it in DocuSign by EOD tomorrow. Michael — I'll draft the doc language and the DocuSign envelope. Lauren — please attach the runbook excerpt so FinLogic can validate the remediation milestones.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
